headline: Ella Gill Joins Somerset Women's Academy
short_post:
![Ella Gill](/images/celebrate-ella.jpg)

Congratulations to Ella Gill on her selection for the Somerset Women's Academy! After outstanding performances in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, including top run scorer for Devon U15 Girls and key contributions to the Devon Women's team, Ella is set to train professionally at the County Ground in Taunton.
full_content:
![Ella Gill](/images/celebrate-ella.jpg)

The past couple of years have been a real turning point for me in my cricketing journey. In the 2024 season, the work that I had been putting into my game was starting to pay off and was becoming evident through the results in my matches. Off the back of a tour to Sri Lanka, I was consistently playing for the U15 Devon Girls team, where at the end of the season I was top run scorer for the team and was leading wicket taker in the regional Counties league. A notable performance for the team was when we bowled Somerset out for 22, where I contributed With bowling figures of 6-6. Throughout this season, I was also training and playing with the Western Storm emerging player programme, which consisted of a pool of players from Devon, Cornwall, Wales, Wiltshire, Somerset and Gloucestershire, aged 14-19. I made two appearances for the EPP against the Army and Central Sparks, which were challenging, but were equally invaluable opportunities to develop my game. Following this season, as a result of the introduction of the new tiered system in the women’s professional game, Western Storm became Somerset and I was selected to be a part of the Somerset EPP, with whom I trained multiple nights of the week during the winter.

The 2025 season brought a new level of challenge to my game, as I began to play at a much higher level. My Devon season consisted of regular matches for the Devon U18 girls, however a large proportion of my season involved me playing for the Devon women’s team for the first time. Playing for this team was one of the highlights of my season and as a result of an unbeaten season in the metro one day cup, we progressed to national finals, where unfortunately we fell short on the day. This season I was also fortunate enough to be called up to play some matches for the Somerset academy. I played against opposition including Surrey, Yorkshire, Glamorgan and Durham were I experienced my first 3 day Game. These matches were a great opportunity to get a feel for the high standard of cricket that is expected at academy and professional level. Moving forward, after an end of season review with Somerset I am very grateful to have been offered an official place in the Women’s academy. I am looking forward to spending the winter training in a professional environment at the County Ground in Taunton to prepare for a full season of tier 1 academy cricket.
